summary: Datadog Logs intake returns 403 for SIEM-ready audit export (API key scoping/permissions)
content:
Issue summary
- Customer reports SIEM-ready audit export (Datadog destination) failing with HTTP 403 responses from Datadog Logs intake.

Impact
- Audit events are not being delivered to Datadog for Helio Health’s beta validation window.
- Customer cannot complete their security validation checklist until events appear in Datadog.

Customer context
- Helio Health (Enterprise). Using Datadog Logs for centralized audit collection.
- Beta feature: SIEM-ready audit export.

Environment
- Redwood: Hosted/Dedicated control plane; exporter running in prod (us-east).
- Destination: Datadog Logs intake.

What we saw (symptoms)
- Exporter adapter reports repeated 403s; retries occur but do not succeed.
- Export lag increases; destination health shows “Auth/permission error”.

Steps to reproduce (from customer)
1) In Redwood Console -> Audit Export -> Add destination -> Datadog.
2) Provide Datadog site = “us1” (datadoghq.com) and API key (redacted).
3) Enable export; within ~1–2 minutes destination health shows failures.

Relevant logs (redacted)
- 2025-04-18T16:22:41Z audit-exporter datadog_adapter request failed status=403 path=/v1/input error="Forbidden" dd_body="{\"errors\":[\"API key is not authorized to submit logs\"]}" tenant=*** dest_id=dd-***
- Note: customer only provided last-4 of key in ticket; full key not captured/stored by Support.

Investigation notes
- Initial hypothesis: wrong Datadog site (us1 vs eu1) or invalid key.
- Verified destination configured for datadoghq.com (us1). Customer confirmed their Datadog org is us1.
- Exporter uses Datadog Logs intake endpoint; 403 indicates key rejected at intake rather than network/TLS.
- Customer confirmed the key works for metrics API in another integration, but logs intake still 403.
- Eng (Logan/Caleb) noted Datadog now supports scoped API keys; if the key is restricted (missing logs ingestion/write scope) intake returns 403.
- Customer checked Datadog UI and confirmed the key was created as a restricted/scoped key intended for API usage, not log submission.

Root cause
- Datadog API key provided to Redwood was scoped/restricted and did not include the permission/scope to submit logs to the Logs intake endpoint, causing Datadog to return 403 Forbidden.

Resolution / recommended remediation (customer-facing)
1) In Datadog, create a new API key that is allowed to submit logs (unrestricted, or explicitly including the Logs ingestion/write scope).
2) Update the Redwood Datadog destination to use the new key.
3) Wait ~2–5 minutes and confirm:
   - Destination health in Redwood Console shows “Healthy”.
   - Audit events appear in Datadog Logs (search by service/source tags used by Redwood; see notes in comments).

Verification
- After customer rotated to a new (unrestricted) API key, exporter status transitioned to Healthy.
- Customer confirmed logs appear in Datadog (sample events: audit categories = authz, workspace, api_key).

Notes / improvements
- Current UI/error messaging shows generic 403; we should surface a clearer hint: “Datadog API key is not authorized for Logs intake (check API key scopes / logs ingestion permission / site).”
- Support guidance: do not request or paste full API keys in Jira; use secure channel if absolutely necessary; last-4 only.

Next steps
- Support: close ticket once customer confirms stable delivery for 24h.
- Product/Eng follow-up: improve docs + Console validation error message for 403 responses from Datadog intake (scope/permission guidance).
comments: 2025-04-18 16:11 (Miguel Santos): Customer (Helio Health) reports Datadog destination failing. Console shows repeated delivery failures, last error “403 Forbidden”. They are blocked on beta validation. Requesting Eng eyes on what 403 typically means for Datadog intake.

2025-04-18 16:26 (Colin O'Donnell): Taking. Can someone confirm whether this is site mismatch (datadoghq.com vs datadoghq.eu) or a key issue? Miguel—please ask customer which Datadog site/org they’re on and whether the key is newly created/scoped.

2025-04-18 16:44 (Miguel Santos): Customer confirmed Datadog site is us1 (datadoghq.com). Key was created by their security team recently; they mentioned they were trying to follow least-privilege and “restricted it to what’s needed.” They assumed logs intake uses same key permissions as other integrations.

2025-04-18 17:02 (Caleb Johnson): Datadog introduced scoped API keys; logs submission can 403 if key doesn’t include logs ingestion/write. Suggest creating an unscoped/unrestricted API key as a test. If that works, it’s definitely key scoping.

2025-04-18 17:19 (Colin O'Donnell): Agree. I’ll send customer steps: generate new API key in Datadog with logs write/ingest allowed, then rotate in Redwood destination. Also remind them to avoid pasting the key in this ticket—last-4 only.

2025-04-19 09:14 (Miguel Santos): Customer rotated to a new key (unrestricted) and updated Redwood destination. Export health flipped to Healthy in ~3 minutes. They can see new events in Datadog Logs. They asked how to filter quickly; I suggested searching by tags and sourcetype/source used by Redwood (I told them to look for “redwood” source/service).

2025-04-19 10:03 (Colin O'Donnell): Great. Marking resolved. Follow-up: our 403 surface is too generic; we should add a hint for scoped-key failures and a docs snippet under Datadog destination setup.
2025-04-20 13:27 (Miguel Santos): Customer confirms delivery stable through weekend test window (no further 403s). Closing.
